page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-32 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the n4d server family. It features 32 dedicated virtual CPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The hardware profile emphasizes memory density over local storage capabilities. Because local storage is absent, workloads requiring persistent or scratch disk space must utilize external block storage volumes, which introduces network-based storage latency considerations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation combined with a high memory-to-core ratio provides a stable resource pool for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of unused local NVMe drives.

This configuration is designed for memory-intensive applications that do not require hardware acceleration. Suitable workloads include in-memory databases, caching layers, enterprise resource planning systems, and large-scale data processing tasks where the working dataset fits within the 256.0 GB memory footprint.
